note: Catalog content for Facets the audit holds out of art generation for carrying nothing but a title. Voice matched to the rows that already have descriptions: dry, specific, present tense, and a turn in the second or third sentence. No 'A type of ...' openers -- the taxonomy column already says what kind of thing it is.

entries.title: Mentor
entries.description: Knows the answer and will not simply hand it over. Depending on the day, this reads as wisdom or as the single most infuriating habit a person can have.

entries.title: Abandoned
entries.description: Places and people left behind, and whatever kept living there afterward. The absence is the subject rather than the setting.

entries.title: Dreams
entries.description: Logic that only holds while you are inside it. Rooms connect wrongly, faces change mid-sentence, and the urgency never names what it is urgent about.

entries.title: Nightmares
entries.description: The same machinery as a dream, but aimed. What it wants is for you to keep looking at it.
entries.flavorText: You know how this one goes. That has never once helped.

entries.title: Tender
entries.description: Care handled carefully. Small gestures, lowered voices, and the specific risk of being gentle somewhere it might not be returned.

entries.title: A former thief seeking redemption.
entries.description: The skills did not leave when the intention changed. Every honest door still shows them exactly where the lock is weak.

entries.title: A wanderer with no memory of their past.
entries.description: Everything before a particular morning is simply missing. They have stopped asking about it and started walking instead.

entries.title: Clone #47 — the one who finally asked "why?"
entries.description: Forty-six of them did not ask. The question had been sitting there the entire time. Nobody had picked it up.
entries.flavorText: Numbers one through forty-six are still working.

entries.title: Once decoded a message hidden in the rain.
entries.description: It turned out to be addressed to them. They have never repeated what it said, and the weather has been notably polite ever since.

entries.title: Was legally adopted by a forest.
entries.description: The paperwork was filed by nobody and holds up regardless. The forest has proven a strict guardian and a fair one.

entries.title: Won a cursed lottery — prize pending.
entries.description: The numbers came up. The prize remains on its way. Everyone involved has quietly stopped describing this as good news.

entries.title: Demi
entries.description: Partially one thing, and the remainder is its own answer rather than a gap. The prefix is doing honest work.

entries.title: Intersex
entries.description: Bodies vary more than the forms have ever allowed for, and always have. The paperwork is the thing that needs updating.

entries.title: Neutrois
entries.description: Neutral by intent rather than by absence. A settled place of its own, not the space between two other places.

entries.title: Pangender
entries.description: All of it, held at once. This is capacity rather than indecision, and the distinction matters to the person holding it.

entries.title: Xenogender
entries.description: Described using things the existing vocabulary does not cover: colour, season, creature, texture, weather. Borrowed words that fit better than the official ones.

entries.title: Androgynous
entries.description: Reads both ways at once and lets the room resolve it. The room frequently does not, which is fine.
entries.flavorText: The pause before someone picks a pronoun is not their problem.

entries.title: Genderqueer
entries.description: Outside the two offered options and comfortable there. The question was the problem, not the answer.

entries.title: Questioning
entries.description: Currently unresolved and fully entitled to be. Notes are being taken. No deadline has been set and none applies.

entries.title: Two Spirit
entries.description: An Indigenous identity carrying its own histories, roles and communities. Not a translation of anything, and not a term for outsiders to borrow.

entries.title: Alien Biologist
entries.description: Cataloguing something that does not fit the taxonomy. Delighted about this. Arguably should be more alarmed than they are.

entries.title: Amazonian Scout
entries.description: Reads the canopy the way other people read street signs. Has not been lost since childhood, and that once was on purpose.

entries.title: Banana Wrangler
entries.description: A genuine posting with a genuine hazard rating. The bananas do not cooperate. People stopped asking follow-up questions years ago.
entries.flavorText: Do not ask about the incident.

entries.title: Cactus Wrangler
entries.description: Moves things that do not wish to be moved and have a direct way of saying so. Thick gloves. Longer patience.

entries.title: Cybernetic Hacker
entries.description: Half the intrusion happens inside their own skull. The wetware is the exploit, and they made peace with that a while ago.

entries.title: Engineer
entries.description: Something is holding. They know precisely which part and precisely how long. Nobody else needs that information yet.

entries.title: Hacker
entries.description: Already inside, and has been for some time. Currently reading the access logs about themselves with professional interest.

entries.title: Nanotech Engineer
entries.description: Works at a scale nobody can watch. The results arrive later and all at once, which looks like magic from every other seat in the room.

entries.title: Pilot
entries.description: Hands relaxed, eyes doing all the work. Conditions outside the cockpit are considerably worse than their expression suggests.

entries.title: Starship Pilot
entries.description: Threading something enormous through something narrow. Has done it before and would rather not specify how many of those times nearly went badly.

entries.title: Atompunk
entries.description: Mid-century atomic optimism. Chrome fins, ray guns, and a fallout shelter sold as a lifestyle upgrade.

entries.title: Bonepunk
entries.description: Technology grown rather than built. Ivory gears, vertebrae scaffolding, machinery that remembers being alive.

entries.title: Clockpunk
entries.description: Renaissance gearwork. Brass escapements, wound springs, and the sketches in the margin actually got built.

entries.title: Desertpunk
entries.description: Sun-bleached survival. Sand-scoured plating, water kept as currency, every surface wrapped against the glare.

entries.title: Doodlecore
entries.description: Ballpoint margins and the back of a receipt. Drawn fast, drawn badly, drawn with total conviction.

entries.title: Etching
entries.description: Fine lines cut into metal and printed in dense black. Every shadow is built from hatching; nothing is shaded softly.

entries.title: Graffiti
entries.description: Aerosol, hard outlines, and letterforms that argue with each other. Made on a wall that was never consulted.

entries.title: Hellpunk
entries.description: Infernal industry. Brimstone smokestacks, chained machinery, damnation reorganised into a supply chain.

entries.title: Junkpunk
entries.description: Assembled entirely from what was thrown out. Nothing matches, every join is visible, and it works. Mostly.

entries.title: Manga
entries.description: Japanese comic linework. Screentone instead of shading, speed lines instead of blur, expressions turned well past realism.

entries.title: Neonpunk
entries.description: Saturated night. Electric pinks and cyans, everything wet enough to reflect them, and no daylight anywhere in frame.

entries.title: Oceanpunk
entries.description: Salt-corroded engineering. Ship hulls repurposed into streets, diving rigs kept running past their rating, everything faintly barnacled.

entries.title: Pastelpunk
entries.description: Rebellion in soft colours. A cotton-candy palette doing something genuinely unsettling and refusing to raise its voice about it.

entries.title: Rococopunk
entries.description: Ornament carried well past the point of sense. Gilt curls, powdered wigs, and a working engine concealed inside a music box.

entries.title: Snowpunk
entries.description: Cold-weather engineering. Furs layered over brass, breath fogging the instrument panel, ice forming in the gears faster than anyone can clear it.

entries.title: Stonepunk
entries.description: Invention at the stone age. Flint mechanisms, log rollers, and technology that was chipped into shape rather than machined.

entries.title: Surrealist
entries.description: Dream logic rendered precisely. Impossible arrangements painted with the flat confidence of a still life, so the eye accepts them before the mind objects.

entries.title: Teapunk
entries.description: Steam's genteel cousin. Porcelain fittings, copper kettles, and machinery that stops entirely for the afternoon.

entries.title: Vaporpunk
entries.description: Sun-bleached digital nostalgia. Marble busts, gridded horizons, and the specific pink of a shopping mall that closed decades ago.

entries.title: Watercolor
entries.description: Pigment moving in water and permitted to do so. Soft blooms, paper texture showing through, edges that let go where they want to.
